clue.text: His offering for your approval is always wet and sometimes dry

definitions.text: His offering for your approval is always wet and sometimes dry

parts.words: His offering for your approval is always wet and sometimes dry
parts.note: a restaurant server who presents a bottle for the diner to taste; what he offers is always liquid, and sometimes a dry vintage

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone whose offerings are always damp and occasionally parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' is the trick: it describes wine that is not sweet, not something free of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: The restaurant steward who brings bottles to the table for tasting is the one whose offering is the drink.

clue.text: A stern view of this ceremony.

definitions.text: A stern view of this ceremony.

parts.words: A stern view of this ceremony.
parts.note: the trail a ship leaves astern is seen from the stern; the same word is a vigil held over the dead

explanation.surface: A severe opinion of a solemn ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stern' looks like 'severe' but is the back of a ship, from which you see the trail in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch kept over a body before burial shares its name with the track a ship leaves behind it.

clue.text: They're so silly in turning up in numbers

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the numbers word

parts.note: nines are numbers

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the little word in from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Foolish people arriving in crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses IN to NI, and 'in' puts it inside NINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpletons or fools are people who are very silly.

clue.text: No part of a brave headdress?

definitions.text: No part of a brave headdress

parts.words: No part of a brave headdress
parts.note: a Native American warrior's war bonnet holds feathers, but the symbol of cowardice would never belong there

explanation.surface: A question about what a warrior's war bonnet would never include.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' suggests a Native American warrior; the feather that marks cowardice would have no place on a courageous man's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale plume handed to a man to brand him a coward is the opposite of a brave's emblem.

clue.text: How one lives and dresses in the row

definitions.text: How one lives and dresses in the row

parts.words: How one lives and dresses in the row
parts.note: one lives in a place, occupying it; split, the word says dressed in monks' robes in their row

explanation.surface: A question about lifestyle and clothing in a terrace of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN HABITS, it means wearing religious robes, like monks lined up in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Occupying a home is to live in it, and dressed in monastic robes is in habits.

clue.text: There's Lee up a damaged shoulder of the bastion

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of lee up a are reordered

explanation.surface: Lee goes up a fortification and hurts his shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up a' look like links but are part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: In fortification, the shoulder of a bastion is the angle where face meets flank, given a French name.

clue.text: What it came to in the old story

definitions.text: What it came to in the old story

parts.words: What it came to in the old story
parts.note: the King James Bible repeatedly says 'and it came to ...', so the phrase completes that old storytelling formula

explanation.surface: A question about how an old tale turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical formula 'And it came to pass' supplies the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Authorised Version of the Bible events are introduced by 'it came to pass', so the word completes the phrase.

clue.text: An egoistic obscurity for a follower of Stahl ?

parts.note: an egoist talks about I, himself
mist obscures things

explanation.surface: A dark, self-centred figure following a German scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: Georg Stahl, an 18th-century German physician, held that the soul animates the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Stahl's doctrine was that a soul drives bodily life, so his disciple believes in spirits behind life.

clue.text: David needed only one of these catapults

definitions.text: David needed only one of these
definitions.meaning: David killed Goliath with a single stone from his sling

explanation.surface: David slew Goliath with just one shot from his catapult.
explanation.definitionFit: David felled Goliath with one stone from his sling, and these Y-shaped hand weapons are catapults.

clue.text: West Side county type

parts.note: by tradition someone born west of the River Medway in Kent has one title, and someone east of it is a Man of Kent

explanation.surface: A New Yorker from the West Side, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Side' suggests Manhattan, but the county is Kent, the English county south-east of London, whose western natives have their own name.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of west Kent is traditionally distinguished by this name from a Man of Kent from the east.

clue.text: Outfit I needed for a Swiss Mountain

parts.note: a rig is an outfit or set of clothes or gear

explanation.surface: Someone choosing clothes for a trip to the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rigi is a well-known peak near Lucerne in central Switzerland.

clue.text: Pine for the 500 dollar question ?

parts.note: a monkey is slang for five hundred, pounds in Britain and dollars in the US
a puzzle is a question to be solved

explanation.surface: Yearning for the answer to a quiz question worth five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb meaning yearn, but it is the tree; MONKEY is slang for 500.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chile pine is a tree with spiky branches thought too hard for a monkey to climb.

clue.text: Scottish kingdom's music-maker

definitions.meaning: the historic Kingdom of ... is a region of eastern Scotland
a small high-pitched flute played in military bands

explanation.surface: The instrument that a Scottish realm is known for.
explanation.definitionFit: The area of Scotland is still called the Kingdom of Fife, and the same word names a small piccolo-like flute.

clue.text: Like a sea of debt ?

parts.note: a sea heaves in great swelling waves; split differently the word is an invoice still unpaid

explanation.surface: Someone drowning in what they owe.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as BILL OWING, a debt still outstanding, while whole it describes a heaving sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough sea swells and surges in great waves, and the same letters describe a bill still to be paid.

clue.text: Substance of a lie about a drink?

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about or concerning
a glass is a drink, as in having a glass

explanation.surface: What a lie told about a drink is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass fibre is a material used in boats and insulation, a substance in its own right.

clue.text: Examines investment in faulty tins

indicators.note: the investment word is placed inside the jumbled letters
something faulty is not in working order, so the letters of tins are rearranged

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a risky investment

explanation.surface: An inspector checks money sunk into defective tin cans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' turns TINS into IN...TS, and 'in' puts SPEC (a speculative investment) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to look it over closely, which is what examining means.

clue.text: One that Dickens roughed out under another name?

definitions.text: One that Dickens roughed out under another name

parts.words: One that Dickens roughed out under another name
parts.note: Dickens's early pieces appeared as ... by Boz, his pen name, and a rough drawing is a quick outline

explanation.surface: A question about a draft Dickens wrote pseudonymously.
explanation.walkthrough: Dickens published 'Sketches by Boz' under the pen name Boz; one of those pieces is also a rough drawing, 'roughed out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough preliminary drawing or short descriptive piece, like those Dickens wrote as Boz.

clue.text: But only two of those animals go on, say

definitions.text: But only two of those animals go on, say

parts.words: But only two of those animals go on, say
parts.note: animals walk on a number of feet that sounds like the answer, but only the front pair are named so

explanation.surface: A remark that animals walk on just two legs.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the word is 'four feet', what animals go on; but only two of the four are the front ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's front feet are its leading pair, the two ahead of the hind ones.

clue.text: Strive to change the plate-holders

indicators.note: the letters of strive are made to change their order

explanation.surface: An effort to alter the things on which dishes stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate-holders' suggests dish racks, but the plates are metal sheets held together by bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal pins hammered through plates hold them together in ships and bridges.

clue.text: I ac's car isn't necessarily of this kind

definitions.text: I ac's car isn't necessarily of this kind

parts.words: I ac's car isn't necessarily of this kind
parts.note: a car can be old without being from the classic early era of motoring

explanation.surface: A remark that an old car is not always a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints '1 ac's car' with 'ac's' in italics; old cars are not automatically from the prized early era of motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cars built in the early prized period of motoring are classed by year, like fine wines from a good year.

clue.text: Dancer who made a poet lose weight ?

parts.note: William Johnson Cory was a Victorian poet, author of 'Heraclitus'
to bant is to diet, from William Banting's slimming regime

explanation.surface: A dancer who got a poet to slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: BANT, from Banting's Victorian diet, is an old verb for slimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A Corybant was a priest of Cybele who worshipped with wild ecstatic dancing.

clue.text: Suitable subject for teaching with an X film ?

definitions.text: Suitable subject for teaching with an X film ?

parts.words: Suitable subject for teaching with an X film ?
parts.note: an X film was an adults-only certificate in Britain; x is also the unknown quantity in school mathematics

explanation.surface: A question about using an adults-only film in class.
explanation.walkthrough: An X certificate marked a British film for adults only; in mathematics x is the unknown, so lessons are full of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The branch of mathematics using letters such as x for unknown numbers is taught with x everywhere.

clue.text: Sounds like a vessel with liquor that went to the head

indicators.note: the word is the one heard when the vessel's name is spoken

parts.note: a cask is a barrel holding drink

explanation.surface: A drink so strong it went to someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went to the head' suggests drunkenness; it means worn on the head, a helmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is armour worn on the head.

clue.text: Stir real egg in drink

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of real egg in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction for whisking an egg into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is part of the letters to stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy soft drink flavoured with root spice is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Part of a surgeon's driving-gear

indicators.note: the answer is a piece of the letters of surgeon's

explanation.surface: A component from a surgeon's car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving-gear' suggests a car part, but it means the force that drives a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong impulse is what drives someone on, so it is their driving force.

clue.text: Noah's son in trouble with some network

indicators.note: something in trouble is upset, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: Shem was one of Noah's three sons

explanation.surface: One of Noah's sons gets caught in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges SHEM, Noah's eldest son in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is a net-like fabric of interlaced threads, a network.

clue.text: Not in a will's corollary

parts.note: the proverb says where there's a will there's a way

explanation.surface: Something missing from a will's consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'where there's a will there's a way' makes 'way' follow from a will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is absent from home or not present is said to be elsewhere, out.

clue.text: Easily grasped (if the answer's a lemon)

definitions.text: Easily grasped (if the answer's a lemon)

parts.words: Easily grasped (if the answer's a lemon)
parts.note: a lemon is pressed for its juice, so grasping it easily means it can readily be pressed

explanation.surface: A comment that an answer is simple to understand unless it is a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasped' suggests understood, but here it means gripped and pressed, as lemons are for juice.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon is pressed for juice, and one that yields to the grip readily is easily compressed.

clue.text: Oblique coping-stone

definitions.meaning: in building, the sloping stone at the foot of a gable's coping

explanation.surface: A slanted stone on top of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means slanting, and in architecture it also names a sloping stone at the base of a gable coping.

clue.text: Failure to… grasp the danger? That sort 'of complaint

definitions.text: Failure to… grasp the danger? That sort 'of complaint

parts.words: Failure to… grasp the danger? That sort 'of complaint
parts.note: the saying is to grasp the stinging plant firmly; brushing it timidly brings an itchy skin complaint

explanation.surface: Someone moaning about not taking a threat seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'grasp the nettle' means tackle a problem boldly; failing to grasp it properly gives you a sting rash.
explanation.definitionFit: The itchy skin reaction caused by stinging plants, a skin complaint, is what a timid touch brings on.
